newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Fremont to acquire Xerox unit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Fremont to acquire Xerox unit.

text.p: California-based workers' compensation insurer Fremont General Corp will gain important geographic diversification with its agreement to acquire Industrial Indemnity Holdings Inc, analysts said.
By expanding outside its California and Illinois strongholds, Fremont will gain increased earnings stability and marketing clout, they said.
"This gives them a lot of firepower in two-thirds of the nation," Dillon Read analyst Michael Lewis said.

The acquisition will provide them "with a little more muscle power in California, Merrill Lynch analyst Jay Cohen said. "Outside of California, it opens up a number of new states for the company," he said.
And that will make the Santa Monica, Calif.-based company less dependent on the California and Illinois workers' compensation markets, Standard & Poor's associate director Matt Coyle said.
He said California and Illinois will represent only about 60 percent of Fremont's book of business after the acquisition compared with more than 80 percent in 1996.
"It adds a measure of strength to their earnings going forward," he said.

Fremont on Monday said it had agreed to acquire Industrial Indemnity from Xerox Corp's Talegen Holdings Inc insurance subsidiary for $365 million in cash and the payment of a $75 million debt obligation Industrial Indemnity has to Talegen.
Fremont rose 2-3/4, or more than nine percent, to close at 31-3/8 on Monday.
Industrial Indemnity was one of five Talegen insurance units buyout firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co had agreed to buy from Xerox in January 1996 for $2.7 billion.
That deal fell apart eight months later. Xerox in January agreed to sell the Coregis Group Inc unit of Talegen to GE Capital for $450 million and that deal is expected to close shortly.
Following Monday's announcement, three insurance units, Crum & Forster, Westchester Specialty and The Resolution Group, remain for sale, Xerox said.
Xerox said the purchase price of Industrial Indemnity is in excess of book value and is consistent with the estimated value of the unit when Xerox discontinued its insurance operations in 1995.
San Francisco-based workers' compensation insurer Industrial Indemnity will expand Fremont General's presence in Arkansas, Hawaii, Arizona, Idaho, Utah, Texas and Oregon in addition to California.
Fremont also expects the acquisition of Industrial Indemnity to add at least about $0.30 a share to 1998 earnings.
Fremont chief financial officer Wayne Bailey said he was comfortable with analysts' 1998 estimates of $3.65-$3.75 a share, compared with previous estimates of about $3.30 a share.
The company also expects to achieve cost savings of $20-$25 million in 1998, Bailey said.
In addition, Fremont will benefit from the acquisition of Industrial Indemnity's roughly $1.2 billion in invested assets.
Analysts said they estimate that could give Fremont another $84 million in investment income in 1998.

Currently, Industrial Indemnity is underwriting annual insurance premiums of approximately $260 million and Fremont's Fremont Compensation Insurance Group, has annual premiums of approximately $480 million.
Goldman, Sachs & Co served as financial advisor to Fremont General Corp. Morgan Stanley served as financial adviser to Xerox.
